Counting Apples Worksheet for Age 4

Age 4 YearsClass 24 · MathsType Printable PDFPlays with the Maths Room

Count the apples in every row, draw exactly the right number into each basket, and trace your numbers.

On the sheet: Count each row, fill the baskets with the right number of apples, trace the numbers.

THE ACTUAL WORKSHEET

Exactly what you’ll print.

This is the real sheet — the same file the buttons above hand you. Title, instructions, the activity itself, and a grown-up answer line where it helps.

Download Free Worksheet ↓ Explore the Maths Room ↗

The PDF is a real printable file (A4, prints fine on US Letter). The print button prints only the worksheet — never the website around it. No sign-up, nothing stored.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Counting rows of apples practices the count-then-write sequence: how many, and what does that number look like? The basket task flips it around — now your child must DRAW a given number, which checks understanding from the other direction.

  • Counting groups of 2 to 5 apples
  • Writing numerals in answer boxes
  • Drawing a given number of objects
  • Tracing numerals 3, 5 and 10
HOW TO USE IT

Three easy steps.

  1. Count out loud together

    Touch each thing as you count it — finger on apple, circle on caterpillar. Touching keeps the count honest.

  2. Write big

    The answer boxes are big on purpose. Big wobbly numerals are exactly what they should be at four.

  3. Check by counting again

    Counting a second time (and getting the same number!) is the skill. Celebrate the recount, not just the answer.

TEACHING TIPS

Little things that help.

Use real things first

Count spoons, steps and apples in the kitchen before the pencil comes out. Numbers live in the world first.

Mistakes are data

If the count comes out different each time, slow down and count as a team. That is the whole lesson.

Keep sessions tiny

One sheet, maybe two rows of it, is plenty for a four-year-old’s counting stamina.

Answer guide

Row counts: 3, 5, 2 and 4. Baskets: 3 apples, then 5 apples. Trace 3, 5 and 10.

WHERE THIS FITS

The class and the game behind it.

This worksheet is the paper twin of Counting Apples. It belongs to Counting & Number Recognition (Class 24) on the Age 4 learning path, and the whole maths collection lives at /worksheets/maths/. Play the game on screen first, print the worksheet second — or the other way round; they practice the same skill in two languages.
